The main issue according to the current bug report is in the "node() implementation in DOM and JDOM model". The problem lies in the DOMNodePointer.java at line 120, where in case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE the code only considers Element and Document nodes as matched by node(), but node() should match any node.

Specifically the current code looks like:
```java
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
    return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

And it should be changed to:
```java
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE:
    return true;
```

This means the code is mistakenly restricting node() matching only to elements and documents, while it should match any node type.

Looking at the failing test `testAxisFollowing()` with the XPath expression `//location[2]/following::node()[2]` which expects to match any kind of node (not just elements or documents) following the second location node, the existing implementation would fail because nodes other than element or document would be incorrectly excluded.

The snippet of DOMNodePointer.asPath() shows code dealing with node types and paths, but the core node test logic for node() is not here. The relevant method for node test is likely within DOMNodePointer but can't be directly found under `nodeTest` method signatures. This suggests that the logic for node matching by nodeTest might be implemented differently or in an internal method or conditional branch.

Thus, the diagnosis is that the node type test implemented for the node() XPath node test is erroneously restrictive, causing the XPath expression in the test (which expects to match all nodes) to fail. Changing the condition to allow all nodes to match will fix the problem.

No recent similar issues are directly related to this node() behavior, confirming that the primary cause is the node type restriction during node() matching inside DOMNodePointer.

# Diagnosis
The bug occurs because the method handling node tests in DOMNodePointer only returns true for element and document node types when testing for node(), excluding other node types like text or processing instructions. This leads to XPath expressions with node() axis tests failing by not matching all node types. The test case fails because `following::node()` expects to match any nodes following the context but current code limits matches. The fix is to change the node test case to always return true for node(), allowing all node types to be matched.

# Next step
The method in DOMNodePointer containing the logic for node type tests (likely a nodeTest or similar named method or a switch/case on Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE) is the best place to fix this bug.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
